# Consul Agentic Runtime Fabric

Consul Agentic Runtime Fabric extends Consul service mesh governance to AI
agents, so that their calls to large language models (LLMs), other agents, and
Model Context Protocol (MCP) tools travel over authenticated, policy-controlled
paths.

@include '../../../global/partials/alerts/beta.mdx'

Consul Agentic Runtime Fabric components run in the Consul control plane and data plane, while applications and external systems keep responsibility for planning, business logic, and user identity.

@include 'alerts/enterprise-alert.mdx'

## Introduction

An AI application can call a model, delegate work to another agent, and invoke tools on behalf of a user. Each interaction requires a distinct decision: whether the workload can connect, whether the user has delegated authority, whether the requested model or tool is permitted, and whether the operation requires human approval.

Consul Agentic Runtime Fabric makes these decisions in gateways, sidecars, and identity integrations that run beside your workloads. It builds on Consul service registration, workload identity, service intentions, and proxy configuration. Consul workload identity and service intentions remain the foundation for mesh connectivity. They do not replace delegated user authorization or application policy.

An AI application remains responsible for planning work, choosing operations, and interpreting results. Network authorization does not establish that an operation is appropriate for a user's task or that a successful response meets the application's requirements.

## Features

| Feature | What it does | Implemented by |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [Governed model access](/consul/docs/agentic-mesh/inference-gateway) | Routes agent requests to models registered in Consul, by capability or by model name, with failover across providers. | AI Inference Gateway |
| [PII protection](/consul/docs/agentic-mesh/inference-gateway#data-protection-and-streaming) | Detects and redacts personally identifiable information in model requests and responses. | AI Inference Gateway |
| [Governed tool access](/consul/docs/agentic-mesh/mcp-sidecar) | Applies per-tool policy to MCP tool discovery and invocation. | MCP Sidecar |
| [Human approval](/consul/docs/agentic-mesh/mcp-sidecar#human-approval) | Holds a protected tool call until a person approves it. | MCP Sidecar |
| [On-behalf-of delegation](/consul/docs/agentic-mesh/identity) | Exchanges a user's token for a token scoped to each destination. | MCP Sidecar and Consul-managed OAuth clients |
| [External credential injection](/consul/docs/agentic-mesh/credential-injection) | Adds a Vault-backed credential to approved external HTTP calls. | Terminating gateway with the Credential Injection Processor |
| [Auto-instrumentation](/consul/docs/agentic-mesh/observability/auto-instrumentation) | Generates trace spans for model and tool calls without application tracing SDKs. | AI Inference Gateway and MCP Sidecar |
| [Cycle detection](/consul/docs/agentic-mesh/cycle-detection) | Finds agents stuck in tool-call loops and rejects their later requests. | Agentic Analytics |

[AI observability](/consul/docs/agentic-mesh/observability) describes the metrics and traces that these components produce.

## Components

| Component | How it runs | Image |
| --- | --- | --- |
| AI Inference Gateway | A gateway deployment for each AI Inference Gateway you define | `csl-inf-rt` |
| MCP Sidecar | A sidecar that Consul injects into AI agent pods. It also runs the OBO identity processor and the human approval server. | `csl-mcp-sc` |
| Credential Injection Processor | A sidecar on a terminating gateway, alongside a Vault Agent sidecar | `csl-au-inj` |
| Agentic Analytics | Services that you deploy for cycle detection | `csl-ag-ana`, `csl-ig-pro`, and `csl-nod-rly` |

To get the images and deploy the components, refer to [Install Consul Agentic Runtime Fabric](/consul/docs/agentic-mesh/install).

## Not included in 2.1

Consul Agentic Runtime Fabric 2.1 does not include a compliance audit trail. For details, refer to [Audit trail](/consul/docs/agentic-mesh/observability#audit-trail).

For the architectural layers and how these components work together, refer to [Consul Agentic Runtime Fabric architecture](/consul/docs/agentic-mesh/architecture).

## Get started

To enable the feature gate and deploy the components, refer to [Install Consul Agentic Runtime Fabric](/consul/docs/agentic-mesh/install).
